title: A study to test how effective Testdrug (AK104) plus lenvatinib is compared with lenvatinib alone in people with advanced liver cancer whose disease has worsened after previous treatment
official: A Phase II, Randomized, Open-label, Multi-center Study of AK104 in Combination with Lenvatinib versus Lenvatinib in Participants with Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma Who Have Progressed on Atezolizumab and Bevacizumab
summary: Main objective: To compare the objective response rate (ORR) of AK104 in combination with lenvatinib versus lenvatinib in participants with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who have progressed on atezolizumab and bevacizumab.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Signed the Informed Consent Form (ICF) voluntarily. This must be obtained before the performance of any protocol related procedures.
2. If participants have HBV or HCV infection, must meet the following criteria: 1) Participants with HBV infection (HBsAg or HBV-DNA positive): HBV-DNA must be <2000 IU/mL and are willing to receive standardized antiviral therapy throughout the study; 2) Participants with HCV infection (HCVAb or HCV-RNA positive): in a stable state judged by investigator; if undergoing antiviral therapy, treatment should continue during the study
3. Adequate organ and hematologic function (within 7 days prior to randomization) NOTE: Other protocol defined Inclusion criteria may apply
4. Age ≥18 years at time of signing ICF.
5. Histologic or cytologic confirmation of HCC, or clinical diagnosis of HCC as per American Association for the Study of Liver Disease (AASLD) criteria.
6. Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage B or C, and not suitable for curative surgical.
7. Participants have progressed on the prior first-line systemic treatment with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab combination treatment.
8. At least one measurable lesion according to RECIST v1.1; or the lesion with previous local therapy can be used as target lesion after the progression is confirmed in accordance with RECIST v1.1.
9. Child-Pugh Class A (within 7 days prior to randomization).
10. ECOG performance status of 0 or 1 (within 7 days prior to randomization)
11. With a life expectancy of ≥3 months.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Known fibrolamellar HCC, sarcomatoid HCC, or mixed cholangiocarcinoma and HCC.
2. Clinically symptomatic or recurrently drained pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, or ascites.
3. History of bleeding event due to esophageal and/or gastric varices within 6 months prior to the first dose of study treatment.
4. The toxic effects of prior anti-cancer treatment have not resolved to NCI CTCAE version 5.0 Grade ≤1.
5. History of malignancy other than HCC within 3 years prior to the first dose of study treatment, except for malignancies with negligible risk of metastasis or death, such as radically treated basal or squamous cell skin cancer, superficial bladder cancer, or carcinoma in situ.
6. History of active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within 2 years prior to the first dose of study treatment (e.g., with use of disease-modifying agents, corticosteroids or immunosuppressive drugs). Replacement therapy (e.g., thyroxine, insulin, or physiologic corticosteroid replacement therapy for adrenal or pituitary insufficiency) is not considered a form of systemic treatment.
7. History of clinically significant cardiovascular disease.
8. Current interstitial pneumonia or interstitial lung disease, or history of interstitial lung disease requiring corticosteroid therapy.
9. History of deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or any other serious thromboembolic condition within 3 months prior to the first dose of study treatment.
10. Has a severe bleeding tendency or coagulation dysfunction, receiving thrombolytic therapy, or is using anticoagulant medications (e.g., warfarin or similar agents) that require INR monitoring. NOTE: Other protocol defined Exclusion criteria may apply
11. Tumor thrombus invasion of superior mesenteric vein, inferior vena cava or more distal veins.
12. Has a known history of, or any evidence of central nervous system (CNS) metastases.
13. Has received anti-cancer therapy for HCC within 3 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment.
14. Has received systemic anti-cancer therapy other than atezolizumab and bevacizumab.
15. Has received herbal or Chinese patent drug with anti-cancer indications or drugs with immunomodulatory effects (including systemic use of thymidine, interferon, interleukin, etc.) within 2 weeks prior to the first dose of study treatment.
16. Has participated in another clinical study within 4 weeks prior to the first dose, unless it is a non-interventional clinical study or a follow-up period of an interventional study (defined as the time from the first dose of the current study being more than 4 weeks after the last dose of the previous clinical study).
17. History of liver transplantation.
18. History of hepatic encephalopathy.
